channel.title: Tech-Economic Times
channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: Surge in software patches likely behind recent tech outages, experts say
item.description: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats Wednesday that there is so far no indication that the tech outages are related. But Clayton said the speed and level of capability of computer systems are "increasing substantially," so legacy computer systems and equipment that already were old are aging much more quickly.

item.title: Arizona says it is investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents
item.description: The state of Arizona has opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday. A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona state law was being violated on an ongoing basis.

item.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the AI giant at $1.5 trillion
item.description: Anthropic decided to barrel ahead with the IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public. Then there's the spectacular downfall of one of the industry's biggest cheerleaders, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
item.description: The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) have discussed the plan, which would apply to companies such as Airbnb, the people said. The company uses Qwen, an AI model made by China's Alibaba , to power its AI customer service agent.

item.title: US, South Korea issue urgent advisories over flaws in Java programming language
item.description: US and South Korean authorities have issued cybersecurity advisories, urging Java users to urgently install security updates after vulnerabilities were found in the popular programming language.

item.title: 'Business as usual': Nvidia's Colette Kress passes first test as board slams door on Huang
item.description: She took the helm last week following news that Huang had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence agencies are investigating over her ties to the Chinese government, revelations that have knocked more than $700 billion off Nvidia's market value.

item.title: US, South Korea issue urgent cybersecurity advisories over flaws in Java programming language
item.description: US and South Korean authorities have issued cybersecurity advisories, urging Java users to urgently install security updates after vulnerabilities were found in the popular programming language.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra, Sol with focus on professional work and cost efficiency
item.description: OpenAI has launched two new artificial intelligence models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, with improved capabilities for professional and everyday tasks, while aiming to reduce the cost of using advanced AI tools for businesses and developers.

item.title: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
item.description: The company had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.

item.title: Anthropic forges ahead with its IPO even as AI fears mount and markets wobble
item.description: No ordinary sale, the Claude chatbot maker's IPO could raise more than $60 billion on Thursday, a massive haul that, depending on the ultimate pricing and other issues, could rival SpaceX's in June.

item.title: "Parlay tech advances into real outcomes": Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella unveils new models for coding, cybersecurity
item.description: Nadella highlighted how the company plans to provide nearly every layer of the technology businesses will need to build, deploy and manage increasingly autonomous AI systems.

item.title: Nvidia expands manufacturing capacity with suppliers to meet AI demand
item.description: Nvidia said on Tuesday it was expanding manufacturing capacity with supply chain partners to support long-term growth in demand for its AI computing platforms.

item.title: Nvidia rejects Jensen Huang's offer to return as CEO despite pressure from Silicon Valley
item.description: The embattled company's board of directors "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of Nvidia's quarterly earnings call before yielding to Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who is running the company as a permanent replacement is sought.

item.title: Nvidia earnings beat estimates; firm won't take questions on resignation
item.description: Nvidia later began a conference call with analysts and investors by saying it wouldn't take questions on longtime CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and doesn't plan to reinstate him. Colette Kress, interim CEO, told investors the company expects revenue to rise 75% in fiscal 2028.

item.title: Beyond the AI hype: How Industrial AI is reshaping India’s factories and infrastructure
item.description: As India moves forward, artificial intelligence technologies are being woven into the fabric of its manufacturing, infrastructure, and transportation sectors. This innovative integration is set to boost productivity and create more sustainable practices, with companies likely to see a drop in engineering timelines and costs through tools like predictive maintenance and automated quality checks.

item.title: Jensen Huang to appear before US House committees on December 1
item.description: The House committees will grill Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter who will appear before Congress on the next day. The scandal surrounding Huang's affair with Alice Huang the alleged Chinese Spy.

item.title: US AI chip curbs threaten Southeast Asia data centre boom, shares slump
item.description: The new rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to the region's major economies such as Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, which some Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models. It also imposes new requirements on overseas data centres that supply "significant volumes of computing power" to firms headquartered in China.

item.title: Samsung Electronics, TSMC shares fall after US announces curbs on China's chip access
item.description: Shares of Samsung Electronics and TSMC lost ground on Tuesday in Asia after the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips.

item.title: Anthropic debuts to skeptics and dogged believers: Mike Dolan
item.description: The Claude developer's bumper initial public offering (IPO) is set to price on Wednesday before trading begins the following day. In the rush to go public before rival ChatGPT owner OpenAI, it has been caught in a volatility storm that's seen some $2 trillion wiped off AI chip giant and ubiquitous AI financier Nvidia's market value in just six weeks.

item.title: Meta says it tuned Instagram to curb suggestive, violent content in India
item.description: Meta Platforms said on Tuesday it had modified Instagram's recommendation systems specifically for India to show less sexually suggestive and violent content, as the government tightens oversight of online content.

item.title: Popular websites subverted in bid to steal crypto, target iPhone users
item.description: Malicious JavaScript was aimed at visitors to the websites of 178 organizations across various sectors through Optimizely, a website optimization platform, according to researcher Scott Helme.

item.title: China taps US AI models to train homegrown rivals as chip curbs bite
item.description: Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic rivals, documents show, as China aims to broaden its AI strategy and offset tightening US curbs on its access

item.title: AI adoption, weak demand to keep India's IT services revenue growth subdued in FY27: Report
item.description: India's IT services sector may continue to face subdued revenue growth in the remaining months of FY27 as rising adoption of artificial intelligence shifts technology spending towards AI-focused companies and reduces demand for traditional services, according to a report by ICICI Securities.

item.title: Study estimates magnitude of US data center pollution as climate talks unveil clean AI pledge
item.description: The pledge also calls for focusing the power of artificial intelligence on solving the so-far intractable problem of climate change and reflects burgeoning concerns about AI's ever-expanding environmental footprint. The political backlash has played out in U.S. elections and major local objections for new sites.

item.title: 98 percent of scientists expect AI to accelerate scientific discoveries, OpenAI study finds
item.description: Artificial intelligence could significantly shorten the time needed for scientific breakthroughs, with 98 per cent of surveyed scientists expecting AI to accelerate discoveries in their fields, according to a new study by OpenAI, highlighting the growing role of tools such as ChatGPT in research.

item.title: Nvidia earnings to test AI boom after Huang's exit
item.description: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, its first since Jensen Huang's departure as CEO, with investors watching for signs of whether the AI boom can withstand the widening scandal that toppled him. Analysts will be watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang's aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

item.title: Singapore seeks 'trusted access' to AI chips after new US curbs
item.description: Singapore said Tuesday it was seeking "trusted access" to advanced AI chips after the United States imposed new curbs aimed at stopping Chinese firms from accessing the technology through overseas data centres. The curbs came days after a spy scandal forced Jensen Huang to quit as Nvidia chief, as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips in violation of US rules.

item.title: California sues OpenAI, seeking court-ordered changes after the Hugging Face hack
item.description: OpenAI announced an "unprecedented cyber incident" on July 21, when its AI agent hacked into another AI company, Hugging Face, after escaping from what was supposed to be an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox. OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face's servers.

item.title: Visa, Mastercard urge approval of $38 billion swipe fee settlement
item.description: * Judge declines to rule immediately, sees 'protracted process' if he rejects settlement * Accord would end 'Honor All Cards' rule, cap fees on standard consumer cards * Opponents say fees remain too

item.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman acknowledges public anger over data centers
item.description: Silicon Valley's pitch to the world about artificial intelligence has missed the mark, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on Monday, nearly two weeks after the US midterms dealt a blow to the industry's data center ambitions. In the midterm elections, voters across the United States approved around 40 new measures restricting or banning new data center development.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO: How do you price the future of AI?
item.description: Speculation over Anthropic' trying to put a price on the future of artificial intelligence. That figure would put the young company among the largest stock market debuts on record, though it falls short of the $2 trillion some estimates had floated until a few weeks ago.

item.title: Fractal in talks with up to 25 AI startups for acquisitions, CEO says
item.description: Enterprise AI firm Fractal Analytics is actively talking to 20 to 25 startups to potentially acquire them, its CEO told Reuters, as it seeks to deepen its vertical-specific capabilities and gain early access to frontier AI models.

item.title: IBM investing $3 billion annually in India, plans $10 billion global quantum push: CEO
item.description: AI could displace 10-20% of jobs over the next decade, with the business process outsourcing (BPO) industry likely to face some of the biggest reductions in employment, Krishna said, arguing that businesses and governments would need to prepare workers for changes in the nature of work.

item.title: Mphasis says clients boost cybersecurity spending as AI-driven threats rise
item.description: Banks and insurers are leading the increase in cybersecurity spending, aided by larger technology budgets and regulatory requirements, while retailers and consumer firms are also stepping up investments to protect customer data, Rakesh said last week, without providing figures.

item.title: SK Hynix to spend $1 billion over five years to support chip suppliers
item.description: South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies

item.title: Jordan blocks Telegram app over national security concerns
item.description: Jordanian authorities said on Monday that they will block the Telegram social media app in the kingdom over national security concerns.

item.title: Intel sued by shareholders following 29% stock plunge
item.description: Intel has been sued by shareholders who accused the US chipmaker of defrauding them by concealing the impact of a prolonged slowdown in personal computer sales that caused its stock price to plunge nearly 29% in a single day.

item.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
item.description: Last week, Germany's Helsing unveiled military intelligence software called Clarity. It is part of a broader market for AI-powered systems designed to accelerate military decision-making by helping sift through vast quantities of data to help identify threats and recommend action, including targeting and attacks.

item.title: Indonesian police raided Nvidia partner Megaspeed's local unit in early 2026 on US request: report
item.description: Megaspeed has been under scrutiny over suspicions it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export restrictions, but there has been no public finding that it has violated the rules.

item.title: DPDP rules may boost demand for cybersecurity professionals and security services: Report
item.description: The implementation of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules is expected to create fresh demand for cybersecurity professionals and managed security services in India, as companies strengthen their systems to protect personal data, monitor security risks and respond to potential data breaches.

item.title: Alibaba unveils new flagship AI model with safety upgrades
item.description: China's Alibaba unveiled its new flagship artificial intelligence model Qwen4-Max on Sunday, saying it enhanced the system's ability to handle complex professional and scientific work while improving protections against safety risks.

item.title: Altimeter, Atreides urge Nvidia board to keep doors open for Jensen Huang's return as CEO
item.description: In a letter addressed to the company's board, Altimeter CEO Brad Gerstner and Atreides Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer Gavin Baker said the board should not rush to appoint a permanent successor before all the facts surrounding Huang's departure are known.

item.title: Microsoft outage shows the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services
item.description: Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. As the outage entered its second day Friday, Microsoft said it saw "encouraging recovery progress." But the company also warned that "intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery" may persist for some users.

item.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
item.description: AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety. But the scandal is unlikely to "dominate the agenda" or affect Trump and Xi's personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore's Nanyang Technological University.

item.title: Softbank further trims India exposure, offloads Meesho shares worth Rs 1,885 crore
item.description: In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to Rs 1,885.17 crore.

item.title: Nvidia approaches Arm Holdings CEO Haas to take over Jensen Huang's job, Elon Musk backs Huang's reinstatement
item.description: According to Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, Haas, who has headed the SoftBank-backed British chipmaker since 2022, is among the names being considered by Nvidia's board as it explores leadership options following Huang's departure.

item.title: Jensen Huang exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
item.description: The projects, stretching from China's wealthy coastal technology hubs to remote western provinces, reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing's access to the technology powering the global artificial-intelligence boom.

item.title: Investors flock to Anthropic IPO but question durability of AI lead
item.description: The Anthropic roadshow is scheduled to run through next Wednesday, when the AI company is expected to price the $64 billion deal. Anthropic and its investment banks are meeting prospective investors in New York, Boston and San Francisco to gauge demand for the offering, one of the people and a third person familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Amazon's plan to own the world's product data and fight AI shopping agents
item.description: Called World Product Graph, the initiative seeks to hoover up data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, whether Amazon stocks it or not, according to an internal document reviewed by Reuters, and to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Simplify Alpha™ opens AI engineering and innovation center in Hyderabad, joined by Simplify Healthcare® and SimplifyX™
item.description: Hyderabad joins Pune and Mumbai as the third India location for the Simplify Group™ companies, adding capacity for customer delivery and growth.
